1. This is a claim for compensation arising out of the Detailed Accident Report filed u/s 158(6)
Motor Vehicle Act, qua petitioner Pitto @ Bhawna for the injuries suffered by her in a vehicular accident which occurred on 30.09.2017 with respect to which FIR No.445/17 U/s 279/338 IPC and 3/181, 146/196, 5/180 MV Act was registered at Police Station Fatehpur Beri and charge-sheet was filed U/s 279/338 IPC and Pitto@Bhawna vs. Sapan Shah and ors. 1/13 3/181, 146/196, 5/180 MV Act against R-1 Sapan Shah, driver of the offending vehicle.

2. The IO has filed copies of the criminal proceedings including FIR and the charge-sheet in the DAR.
3. Brief facts of the vehicular accident as averred in the DAR are that on 30.09.2017, the petitioner alongwith her minor daughter namely Bhawna @ pitto @ Kittu were going on foot.

4. The respondent no. 1 driver of the motorcycle has contested the claim by filing his WS stating therein that he was driving the motorcycle in a very safe and cautious manner.
When he reached near the spot, the injured Pitto suddenly came infront of his motorcycle after leaving the hand of her mother which led to the collision.
As soon as the respondent noticed the sudden movement of the claimant towards the motorcycle, he tried to stop but could not avoid the collision, despite the slow speed of the motorcycle.
He further submitted that the claimant's mother was negligent in leaving her child unattended while walking on the road.

6. After completion of the pleadings, vide order dated 27.01.2020 following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor:-
1.

Whether petitioner Ms. Bhawna sustained injuries in the road accident on 30.09.2017 at about 6.45 am at Tempo Stand Jonapur, New Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle Motor cycle bearing no. DL-3SCU-0203 being driven by respondent no. 1 Sh. Sapan Shah and owned by respondent no. 2 Sh.
Devender?
OPP 2.
To what amount of compensation the petitioner is entitled and from whom?

3. Relief.
7.
I have heard Ld. Counsels for the petitioner and have carefully perused the court record.

My findings on the issues are as under:-
8.

In a claim petition, onus is on the claimant(s)/ petitioner(s) to prove that the injured suffered injuries in a vehicular accident caused by the wrongful act or negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
9. In order to establish her claim, Smt. Mithlesh Devi (mother of the injured and also the eye witness) examined herself as PW1 and deposed on the lines of her claim.
She stated in her affidavit in evidence Ex.PW1/A that she is the mother of the petitioner/injured.

On 30.09.2017 at about 18.45 hrs, the petitioner/injured namely Bhawna @ Pitto @ Kittu D/o Sh. Pramod Kumar aged about 7 years was going on foot Pitto@Bhawna vs. Sapan Shah and ors. 3/13 alongwith her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

When they Pitto (Dar) vs Sapan Shah (Fir-445/17, P.S-F.P. Beri) on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171853206/
2 reached at Tempo Stand, Jonapur, New Delhi, all of a sudden one motorcycle bearing no.
DL-3SCU-0203 came in a very high speed which was driven by the driver in a rash and negligent manner hit the daughter of the PW1 due to which she fell down on the road and sustained multiple injuries.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She was removed to Trauma Centre, AIIMS Hospital where MLC was prepared.
At the time of accident her daughter was studying in the class 1 st -B in a Local Public School.

She has tendered her affidavit in evidence in support of her contention :-
 Copy of MLC of the petitioner/minor Ex.PW1/1.  Original discharge summary of the petitioner/ minor Ex.PW1/2.  Copy of school identity card of the petitioner alongwith the DAR Ex.PW1/3.
 Copy of the aadhar card of the petitioner with the DAR Ex.PW1/4.  DAR Ex.PW1/5.
 Copy of the aadhar card of the deponent Mark X

After the examination in chief of the PW1, the respondent no.
(s) 1 and 2 were proceeded ex-parte on 28.11.2023 as they were not appearing for many hearings.
PW1 was never cross-examined by them.

10. In the present case, the Investigating Officer had filed the DAR containing FIR, Charge sheet,
site plan, MLC etc.
Charge sheet has been filed against the respondent no.1.
PW1 Mithlesh Devi had categorically deposed the fact about the occurrence of the accident due to rash and negligent driving of the Respondent No.1.
No other version of accident has come on record except the one as narrated PW1.
The statement of the PW1 that the offending vehicle hit her minor daughter Bhawna @ pitto finds support with the fact that the I.O. seized the offending vehicle and got it mechanically inspected.

Counsel for the petitioners has argued forcefully that from Pitto@Bhawna vs. Sapan Shah and ors. 4/13 the evidence of PWs coupled with the criminal record placed, the petitioners have proved the fact that it was the respondent who had caused the accident by his rash and negligent driving.

sentences.text: 12. DAR and copies of criminal proceedings filed alongwith it are admissible in evidence and deemed to be correct under Rule 7 of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Rules, 2008 until proved to be contrary.
Copies of criminal proceedings filed include FIR, chargesheet, site plan, MLC of the petitioner, mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle besides the documents of the offending vehicle.
Copies of criminal proceedings filed alongwith it have not been challenged and controverted by any of the respondents.

13. In this regard observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana and Ors. reported in 2007 SCC online DEL 1700 has to be considered wherein it was held that :-

3

sentences.text: " the wife of the deceased had produced (1) certified copy of criminal record of criminal case in FIR No. 955/2004 pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle; (2) Criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge-sheet under Section 279/304-A IPC against the driver; (3) certified copy of FIR wherein criminal case against the drive was lodged; and (4 ) recover memo and mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.

These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent."
14.
It is a settled legal position that while deciding a petition u/s 166 of the M V Act, the Claims Tribunal has to decide negligence on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.

Reference in this regard is made to the observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pitto@Bhawna vs.
Sapan Shah and ors. 5/13 Kaushnumma Begum and Others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, 2001 ACJ 421 SC, wherein it was held that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of motor vehicle involved in the accident is of secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injuries or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable u/s 166 & 140 of the M V Act.
15.

sentences.text: 16. PW1 Smt. Mithlesh Devi, mother of the injured Pitto @Bhawna has clearly deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving it rashly and negligently.
Her deposition on this fact has gone unrebutted by respondents who have not even cared to cross- examine her.

17. According to MLC of the petitioner filed on record, the injured was taken to JPN Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMS, New Delhi with the alleged history of road traffic accident and nature of injury is mentioned on the MLC as 'grievous'.
MLC has not been challenged by the respondents about cause and nature of injury.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that the respondent no. 1/ driver of the offending vehicle was the material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of the inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
19. The deposition of the petitioner about the manner of accident is also corroborated by the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle.

The damages on the offending vehicle has Pitto (Dar) vs Sapan Shah (Fir-445/17, P.S-F.P. Beri) on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171853206/
4 never been explained by respondent no. 1.

sentences.text: From the mechanical inspection report produced on record it is found that there are damages due to accidental impact on the offending vehicle which corroborate the version of the petitioner.

20. On the basis of evidence on record, above observation and discussion it is proved that the abovesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of R1 Sapan Shah due to which injured Pitto @ Bhawna suffered grievous injuries.

Also in the absence of any defence brought on record by R1, R2 and unrebutted testimony of PW1 Smt. Mithlesh Devi corroborated by criminal proceedings the fact that the offending vehicle hit the petitioner prima facie shows rash and negligent conduct of R1.
21.

On the basis of above observation and discussion it is proved that the abovesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of R1 Sapan Shah due to which petitioner Pitto @Bhawna suffered grievous injuries.
Issue no. 1 is accordingly, decided in favour of the petitioner.

Pitto@Bhawna vs. Sapan Shah and ors. 7/13  Findings on Issue no.2:
To what amount of compensation, the petitioner is entitled and from whom?
22.

sentences.text: Now, the court has to assess as to how much compensation be awarded to the claimant and by whom?
First of all the court has to decide as to whom the liability to pay the compensation is fastened.
22. As the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 therefore, primary liability to compensate the petitioner is that of respondent no. 1.
As the offending vehicle was owned by respondent no. 2 therefore, he becomes vicariously liable to compensate the petitioner.
It is an admitted position on record that the offending vehicle was not insured.
Therefore, the liability to compensate the petitioner would remain with respondent no(s). 1 and 2 jointly and severally.
23. Now the Court has to decide the compensation which the injured is entitled.
Injured in road traffic accident is entitled to damages for the injury suffered by her arising out of use of Motor Vehicle under both non-pecuniary and pecuniary heads.

MEDICAL EXPENSES :
24.
As per the record, no medical bills were filed by the petitioner.

PAIN AND SUFFERINGS AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE :
25.
As per the discharge summary, the petitioner was diagnosed with head injury and RT Upper Lung Contusion.
The injured remained admitted in Jai Prakash Narayn Apex Trauma Centre Hospital from Pitto@Bhawna vs. Sapan Shah and ors. 8/13 02.10.2017 to 07.10.2017.

SPECIAL DIET, CONVEYANCE AND ATTENDANT CHARGES :
26.
In the present case the petitioner has not placed on record any document with regard to special diet, conveyance and attendant charges.
However, the injuries on her person were such that she must have taken special diet for her early recovery.
She must have spent some amount on conveyance and attendant.
Therefore, looking into all the facts, I award Rs.30,000/- to the petitioner towards special diet, conveyance and attendant charges.

LOSS OF STUDY :
27.
At the time of accident, the injured was aged about 07 years.
PW1 stated in her affidavit that at the time of accident his daughter was studying in 1st Class in Aroma Pubilc School, Jonapur, New Delhi.
Due to the injuries, she could not attend the school for a certain period, therefore, I award a lumpsum amount of Rs.30,000/- to the injured towards the loss of study.

28. The total compensation in favour of the petitioner is assessed as under :
 MEDICAL EXPENSES : Nil  PAIN & SUFFERINGS & ENJOYMENT  OF LIFE :Rs. 70,000.00  SPECIAL DIET, CONVEYANCE  & ATTENDANT :Rs. 30,000.00  LOSS OF STUDY :Rs. 30,000.00  ===========

 ===========
 RELIEF 29.

In view of my findings on the issues, I award a sum of Rs.1,30,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Thirty Thousand only) to petitioner Pitto@ Bhawna as compensation along-with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing the DAR till its realization.
Since the petitioner is minor, hence the awarded amount be released to her mother Mithlesh Devi being her natural guardian.
30. The respondents are directed to credit the amount directly to the MACT account of State Bank of India, District Court, Saket branch.

12. DAR and copies of criminal proceedings filed alongwith it are admissible in evidence and deemed to be correct under Rule 7 of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Rules, 2008 until proved to be contrary.
Copies of criminal proceedings filed include FIR, chargesheet, site plan, MLC of the petitioner, mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle besides the documents of the offending vehicle.
Copies of criminal proceedings filed alongwith it have not been challenged and controverted by any of the respondents.
It is a settled legal position that while deciding a petition u/s 166 of the M V Act, the Claims Tribunal has to decide negligence on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Reference in this regard is made to the observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pitto@Bhawna vs.
Sapan Shah and ors. 5/13 Kaushnumma Begum and Others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, 2001 ACJ 421 SC, wherein it was held that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of motor vehicle involved in the accident is of secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injuries or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable u/s 166 & 140 of the M V Act.
15.
Nevertheless, it is also a settled legal position that in a claim petition u/s 166 of the M V Act,
burden is on the claimants/petitioners to prove negligence.
The law to this effect was declared in Minu B Mehta Vs. Balkrishna Ramchandra Nayan (1977) 2 SC 441 was reiterated by the Supreme Court in Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs. Meena Variyal 2007 (5) SCC 428, which has been followed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in a recent case, New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Devki &
Ors., MAC APP 165/2013 decided on 29.02.2016.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
22. As the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 therefore, primary liability to compensate the petitioner is that of respondent no. 1.
As the offending vehicle was owned by respondent no. 2 therefore, he becomes vicariously liable to compensate the petitioner.
It is an admitted position on record that the offending vehicle was not insured.
Therefore, the liability to compensate the petitioner would remain with respondent no(s). 1 and 2 jointly and severally.
23. Now the Court has to decide the compensation which the injured is entitled.
Injured in road traffic accident is entitled to damages for the injury suffered by her arising out of use of Motor Vehicle under both non-pecuniary and pecuniary heads.
However, the injuries on her person were such that she must have taken special diet for her early recovery.
